en: Now, when building software on top of AI
models, we're no longer using ChatGPT or
Claude. We're no longer using these tools.
Instead, we're writing or generating with AI
our own code. And in that code, we may want
to use the OpenAI models or the Anthropic
models. We may want to build our own
application on top of AI. And we can do
this. All these model providers do
offer their models for use in your software
through something called an API, an
Application Programming Interface, which
simply means an endpoint, an address in the
World Wide Web, you could say, your software
can send a request to, to get back an
answer. So it's the programmatic form of
using ChatGPT, if you wanna call it like
this.
Those APIs, those endpoints offer you a lot
of settings you can set and tweak. And that
allows you, if you're building your own
software, software to make sure that you are
getting exactly the response you want to get
back. Now, as a side note, it's also this
approach that allows you to define your own
tools, for example, because these AI models,
they are quite capable at making decisions.
And if you tell them, hey, you got a certain
tool available, depending on the prompt they
received, they may decide to use that tool
to complete that task. If you're using the
ChatGPT app or the Claude app or anything
like that,
you can't define your own tools. These
applications already have predefined tools,
tools to read your local file system, for
example. And that's then sent behind the
scenes to that same API. But if you're
building your own program, you can have that
control and you can build your own very
powerful applications on top of these AI
models therefore. And we'll get back to this
entire tool part once we dive a bit deeper
into agents.
